title: Bouncing ball

slow_motion.evidence: no caption or effect indicating slow motion

subjects.description: small round orange ball with white highlight

observation.what_happens: An orange ball falls from the upper left toward the brown floor and bounces. It then continues rightward across the frame with successive bounces while airborne between impacts.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 356 px/s² over 4 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x grows almost steadily while y falls and rebounds twice with lower peaks, so horizontal force is tiny and vertical motion is gravity plus impact loss. These three candidates test no air vs viscous vs realistic squared drag with floor restitution and friction for the unseen bounces.

law.title: Gravity only with bouncy floor
law.summary: The ball flies like a cannonball with only gravity pulling down and loses a fixed fraction of up-speed on each floor hit.

Spin and sideways scrub at impact are ignored.
critique.finding: The ball falls pulled by {g} and hits the floor at {y_floor}, keeping {e} of its bounce speed each time.
critique.headline: Orange ball falls under gravity and keeps bouncing.
critique.why_it_won: It captures every bounce cleanly, while adding air drag does not improve the future path at all.

headline: Orange ball falls under gravity and keeps bouncing.
finding: The ball falls pulled by 9.81 m/s² and hits the floor at -7.68 ± 0.0036 m, keeping 0.85 ± 1.97e-4 of its bounce speed each time.

eyeball.law_in_words: the ball centre at contact is one radius above the floor, and normal restitution is outgoing over incoming normal speed, so rebound peak height scales as e squared times drop height
